function.name: energy_calculator_calculate
function.description: Calculate the energy needed to heat a substance from an initial to a final temperature. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in grams. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degrees Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degrees Celsius. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit to report the energy in. Options are 'joules' and 'calories'. Defaults to 'joules'.

message.content:
**Energy needed to raise the temperature**

The heating energy \(Q\) is calculated with  

\[
Q \;=\; m\,c\,\Delta T
\]

where  
\(m\) – mass (grams),  
\(c\) – specific‑heat capacity (\(\text{J g}^{-1}\!\!^\circ\mathrm C^{-1}\)),  
\(\Delta T\) – change in temperature (degrees C).

| Substance | Specific heat \(c\) | Mass \(m\) | Temperature rise \(\Delta T\) | Energy \(Q\) |
|-----------|---------------------|------------|---------------------------------|--------------|
| **Water** | \(4.186~\text{J g}^{-1}\!\!^\circ\mathrm C^{-1}\) | \(100~\text{g}\) | \(100 - 25 = 75^{\circ}\mathrm C\) | \(100\times4.186\times75 = 31,\!395~\text{J}\) |
| **Aluminium** | \(0.900~\text{J g}^{-1}\!\!^\circ\mathrm C^{-1}\) | \(100~\text{g}\) | \(75^{\circ}\mathrm C\) | \(100\times0.900\times75 = 6,\!750~\text{J}\) |

---

### Results

- **Heating 100 g of water from 25 °C to 100 °C:** ≈ **31 kJ** (31 395 J).
- **Heating 100 g of aluminium under the same conditions:** ≈ **6.7 kJ** (6 750 J).

These values assume constant specific heats over the temperature range and neglect phase changes or other losses.
